Śākyamuni did not appear in this world; Bodhidharma did not come from the West. The Buddha-dharma pervades the entire earth; yet when discussing the profound mystery, the mouth remains closed.
At that time, the traces of speech and writing did not arrive; the sharp edges of the kōan-encounters involving staffs and shouts were not revealed.

Yet, when the flower was held up for the assembly, dragging forth the withered and rotten vines of old, and when the snow was stood in to settle the mind, the present-day public case suddenly emerged.
Thus, the wind of the school was widely propagated and the sun of wisdom hung high; the lamp of the long night was lit, and the masses of the ignorant were instantly awakened.
Holding up a single blade of grass, the entire Dharma-realm is viewed as one; to drive a carriage, one must strike the ox. How could grinding a tile produce a mirror?
Like a single grain of elixir that transforms iron into gold, a single word of ultimate truth transforms the ordinary into the sage.

The six generations of patriarchs shattered reflections in the water, so that everything met by the eye was the Real. The five schools vied with each other like flowers in the sky; their whole being was nothing but courage.

He rushed out sideways. He laughed at how a wooden stump could endure such treatment; with a sudden lift of his robes he turned back, realizing that the Buddha-dharma is not something vast or complex.

Seeing the reflection in the water, he did not seek it elsewhere; wherever he encountered it, he met "him. With his legs severed, he saw his own faults through the pain; in every instance, there was the Way.
If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, everything is already fully accomplished. To examine closely this profound principle is like a thousand lamps illuminating one another. Dragons and snakes—
Distributed beneath the staff, the ordinary and the holy alike rely upon it to pass through. The triggering of the faculty occurs before any sign has manifested;

its application extends beyond form and sound. Even a single word of praise or censure, a single phrase of right or wrong, a subtle penetration with a single finger, or the bestowing and seizing with a single blow—taking what is wrong as right, the mouth seems sweet while the intent is bitter; taking what is right as wrong, the heart is truly...
Having granted this, my words fall short of full expression. Although I have long associated with the venerable elders, I do not dare to gaze upon them with the "correct eye" (zhengyan);

how much less could the pathways of intellectual understanding and conscious discernment ever penetrate it? Therefore it is said: those with wild faculties and inferior understanding cannot be shown the Great Dharma, nor can they hear the Vehicle of the Patriarchs.
It is like placing fine food into a foul vessel. Did the Patriarch not say: "The finest clarified butter (tihu)..."?
Flavors are prized by the world; yet when encountered by such people as these, they instead become poisonous medicine. Only those with great resolve can bear this burden.

Originally, Bodhidharma traced his lineage back to the Great Tortoise Lord from Śākyamuni Buddha, when [the Buddha] blinked his blue-lotus eyes.
He was the twenty-eighth patriarch who attained the essence of the "separate transmission outside the teachings.

Having received the Buddha’s mind-seal, he arrived in the Eastern Continent (China) at the beginning of the Putong era of the Liang dynasty. At that time, scholars were preeminently distinguished for their exegesis and meditation;

he therefore declared: "I do not rely on words and letters; my school consists of directly pointing to the human mind, so that one may see one's nature and become a Buddha. This lineage was transmitted six times until...
The Great Mirror of Caoxi branched out into Nanyue and Qingyuan; these further divided into the five schools of Yunmen, Linji, Caodong, Guiyang, and Fayan.
These branches and lineages spread extensively throughout the world. Master Guifeng Zongmi’s *Chan Yuan Chui* states:
"There are five categories of Chan: first, the Chan of external paths; second, the Chan of ordinary persons; third, the Chan of the Small Vehicle..."
There are four types of meditation: what is called Mahāyāna meditation, and what is called the Meditation of the Supreme Vehicle (*agrayāna*).
As for the practices of the eminent monks of antiquity and that which other schools refer to as "Chan," these all belong to the first four types of meditation.

Only that which was transmitted through successive generations by Bodhidharma is identical to the Buddha-body from the very outset; it stands far apart from all other gateways. This is indeed the Meditation of the Supreme Vehicle. —Ziyang Zhu Wen Gong.
It is said: "Dharma [Master] completely overturned the old molds and established the Chan School; his approach was far more sublime than that of the scholastic study of doctrine (yixue).
It is further said: "He gazes upon and points to the nature and mind; his names and words transcend both existence and non-existence.

From this, one knows that Master Wen deeply understood the purport of the separate transmission (biezhuan), which is essentially beyond the reach of verbal instruction. People of the world merely see Master Wen’s words regarding defending the Way and establishing the teachings.

Yet, regarding our school, they have not been able to catch even a glimpse of its excellence or taste a single morsel of its essence, and they nonetheless indulge in reckless denigration; this is because they do not understand the Master.
Recently, a man from Zhejiang named Huang, who prides himself on his extensive learning, has claimed that the "separate transmission outside the teachings" is not the doctrine of the Buddha.
To treat this as a separate school is, alas, to claim the title of a "universal Confucian" (tongru); it makes one a true culprit against Master Zhu.

The Way of the Separate Transmission is fundamentally beyond words; yet, the Way must be manifested through words. Even though Śākyamuni Buddha possessed such clear and profound awakening, he still received the prediction and seal of approval from Dīpaṃkara.
Thus, we know that the pivotal sayings through which the patriarchs transmitted the Dharma from one to another could not have been left unrecorded.
Thus it was. During the Jingde era of the Song dynasty, the monk Daoyuan of Wuzhou compiled the *Chuan Deng Lu* (Record of the Transmission of the Lamp).

Emperor Zhenzong summoned the Hanlin Academician Yang Yi to edit and compose its preface. During the Tianxing era, Li Zunxu, the Prince Consort, produced the *Guang Deng Lu* (Extended Record of the Lamp), for which Emperor Renzong composed the imperial preface.
In the first year of the Jianzhong Jinggu era, Chan Master Baizhang Foguo completed the *Xu Deng Lu* (Continued Record of the Lamp).

Recorded. Emperor Huizong composed the preface. In the tenth year of the Chunxi era, Chan Master Ming of Jingci, known as Huiweng, compiled the *Lian deng huiyao* (Essentials of the Linked Lamps), which was prefaced by Li Yong of Danzhai.
During the JiaTai era, Chan Master Shou of Leian compiled the *Pudeng lu* (Universal Lamp Record), which Lu You wrote the preface for.
These five lamp records trace the origins [of the lineage] and were transmitted alongside the canonical scriptures until the end of the Song dynasty. Da Chuan of Lingyin...

He therefore compiled the *Wudeng Huiyuan* for his disciples to benefit future students; his kindness was most profound.

those who understand this regret it. The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* states: "The World-Honored One emitted light from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows, its radiance illuminating eighteen thousand worlds in the eastern direction.
Maitreya posed questions, and Mañjuśrī resolved the doubts," regarding [the Buddha] as the Sun-Moon-Lamp.
The auspicious signs of the Buddha’s original light are thus clarified. The *Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa Sūtra* states: "There is a dharma-gate called the 'Inexhaustible Lamp.
As for the Inexhaustible Lamp, it is like a single lamp that kindles hundreds of thousands of lamps; those who were in darkness all become illuminated, and this illumination never comes to an end.

"What is the meaning of this? Jifu asked. Jiufu replied, "The sun and moon alternate with one another to provide illumination, yet they cannot shine simultaneously.

That which can rival the brilliance of the sun and moon to dispel all darkness is only the lamp. I have recorded this for him. This year the Duke reached the age of eighty. He often lamented that the woodblocks for the *Wudeng huiyuan* had been destroyed, leaving scholars with no means to consult or verify the pivotal words and teachings of the Buddhas and patriarchs.
Thereupon, he exhausted the resources of his robes and almsbowl to initiate a campaign for donations.
This was undertaken by the Grand Marshal, Minister of State, Peer of the Court, Pillar of State, and Acting Provincial Secretary of the Jiangxi and Zhejiang regions.
The Duke of Kangle, Chief Chancellor concurrently presiding over the Court of Military Affairs and leading the Court of Imperial Sacraments, was the first to donate his stipend.
Upon hearing this, the various masters of Wu and Yue unanimously supported him. Once the woodblocks were completed, he sent his disciple Miaoyan to request a preface for the work.
I regard Master Qing as my paternal uncle; indeed, I once received his instruction.

Admonition. I have admired his lofty character. Now, as Master Yue’s benevolence has enabled the aspirations of those who come to study here to be fulfilled, I have not declined to compose this preface despite its rusticity and my own seclusion. Thus it is said.
